messages.content: i am taking a train to see my aunt tomorrow morning. i want to bring something to eat, but i do not want to carry much.
what food do you already have that is easy to carry and eat on the way?
i have bread, cheese, and some fruit. my aunt says lunch will be ready when i get there.
then you may only need a little food for the journey, rather than a whole lunch. bread and fruit could be a simple choice if those are things you want to eat.
can you give me a shorter answer?
you could bring a little bread and fruit for the journey, because lunch will be ready at the visit.
i keep feeling worried that i will be hungry even though the journey is short.
you can use what you know about the time before lunch to choose enough food for the journey. a small plan can still leave room for what you need.
say it with fewer words.
use what you know about how long the journey takes to choose how much food to bring.
write me a short list with just the food i chose.
you have not chosen the food yet. would you like the list to be bread and fruit?
yes, just that.
bread and fruit.
the walk to the house of my friend takes ten minutes. i want to be there at the time we chose, but also have five quiet minutes before going inside. how early should i leave?
leave enough time for the ten minute walk and five quiet minutes before the visit. that is five minutes more than the walk alone.
do i have to add ten more minutes because the walk is ten minutes?
no. you asked for five quiet minutes, not another full walk. you need the ten minute walk and then the five quiet minutes.
give me a more simple explanation.
you need ten minutes to walk and five minutes to sit before the visit.
can you write that using no number word above ten?
leave home with time for a ten minute walk and five quiet minutes before the visit.
what if the walk takes longer today?
then you may have less quiet time before the visit. if you know the walk could take longer, leave more time before the visit.
give me a simple last answer.
if the walk may take longer, leave more time before the visit.
write a story about someone doing a small kind thing without getting anything large back for it.

a boy saw his neighbor trying to open her door while holding food and a book. he asked if he could hold the book for a moment. she said yes. he held it while she opened the door, then gave it back. she said thank you, and he went home. at dinner, he told his father what happened. his father asked if helping had been useful. the boy said yes, because the neighbor could use her hand for the door while he held the book.
tell it more simply.

a boy saw his neighbor trying to open her door while holding food and a book. he asked if he could hold the book for a moment. she said yes. he held it while she opened the door, then gave it back. she said thank you, and he went home.
did she give him the book to keep?
no. he held it while she opened the door, then gave it back.
why did he ask before taking it?
asking gave her a choice about whether she wanted that help.
what did she say at the end?
thank you.
my friend is going to live in another town. i want a goodbye message that is warm but not as if we can never talk again.
you could say you will miss seeing her often and that you would like to keep writing or calling. the move changes where she lives, not whether you can care about each other.
write a short message in simple words.
i will miss seeing you here, but i am happy we can still talk. i hope the new town feels like home soon.
what if i am not happy about the move yet?
then do not make the message say you feel something you do not. you can be sad about the change and still wish her well.
give me a message with sad in it.
i feel sad that you are leaving, and i will miss seeing you. i hope things go well in your new town. let us keep talking.
can i say nothing will change?
that might not be true. where she lives and how often you meet may change. you can say you want to stay close without saying everything will be the same.
keep the last answer simple.
you can say you still want to talk and care about her. you do not need to say every part will stay the same.
i can sing the middle of a song, but i keep starting it wrong because i cannot remember the first line.
you could work on the first line by itself, then sing it with the next part. that gives you a clear place to begin when you start the whole song.
i forgot the first line again today.
then you can try the first line again today without saying the rest of your learning is gone. you still know the middle part.
my friend knows the first part. could i ask her to sing it with me?
yes. you could ask her to sing the first line slowly, then let you try it before going on.
give me the question i can ask.
could you sing the first line slowly with me, then let me try it on my own?
what if she gives me the whole song too fast?
you can ask for just the first line again. being specific about the small part you need can make the help more useful.
write that request.
please sing only the first line for now. i would like to learn that part before the whole song.
just tell me the first thing to work on.
the first line.
in my picture, a woman gives a book to a girl. i wrote she was happy. is it clear who felt happy?
not by itself. she could mean the woman or the girl. you can use the full word for the person you mean.
i mean the girl who got the book.
then you could say: the girl was happy when the woman gave her the book.
give me only the sentence with that meaning.
the girl was happy when the woman gave her the book.
what if i want both people to be happy?
you could say: the woman and the girl were both happy.
is both enough by itself if someone does not know who i mean?
no. it helps to make clear which two people both is about. your full sentence can do that.
give me a more simple explanation.
you need to make clear which two people you mean. the woman and the girl were both happy does that.
write one sentence that gives the book and both feelings.
the woman gave the girl a book, and both were happy.
my cousin told me the library is open tomorrow. i want to ask what time, but she says that must mean i do not believe her.
you can believe that it is open and still need the time. those are different details.
write a short answer to her that is kind.
i believe you that it is open. i just need to know the time so i can plan my visit.
what if she does not know the time?
then you both know one part and not the other. you can look for the time without changing what she already told you.
say it another way.
you can find out the time while keeping the information that the library is open.
should i ask whether it will be open every day of the year too?
only if that is important for the visit you want. for tomorrow, the useful question is the time tomorrow.
use only the words we have and give me just that question.
what time will the library be open tomorrow?
write about a child who wants to help someone but first needs to finish a short task.

a girl was writing the last line of a letter when her brother asked if she could help him find his book. she wanted to help, but she did not want to lose her place in the letter. she asked if he could wait a minute while she finished the line. he said yes and looked by his chair while waiting. when she put her writing tool down, she asked where he had last seen the book. together, they checked the table and found it under a piece of paper. she was happy she had asked for a little time to finish her work before helping.
give me only the part about what they found and how she felt.
she put her writing tool down and helped him look. they found the book under a piece of paper on the table. she was happy she had asked for time to finish her line first.
did asking him to wait mean she would not help?
no. she asked for a minute before helping, not to leave him without help.
what did she ask when she was ready?
where he had last seen the book.
was it under his chair?
no. it was under a piece of paper on the table.
write about a room using only these facts: a blue chair is by the window, a table is in the middle, and a book is on the table.
a room has a blue chair by the window and a table in the middle. a book is on the table.
can you make it sound like a quiet bedroom?
bedroom and quiet would add details you did not give. do you want those to be new story details, or do you want to keep only the original facts?
i want no new facts.
then keep the words about the chair, window, table, and book. the facts do not say what kind of room it is or what can be heard there.
give me just one sentence.
a book is on the table in the middle of the room, and a blue chair is by the window.
what color is the table?
you have not given its color.
can i say the book is blue because the chair is blue?
no. the color of the chair does not tell us the color of the book.
write one question that would get that detail.
what color is the book?
put the reason first in this sentence: i stayed home because i wanted to finish my book.
because i wanted to finish my book, i stayed home.
now put the part about what i did first again.
i stayed home because i wanted to finish my book.
what was the thing i did?
you stayed home.
and what was the reason i gave?
you wanted to finish your book.
does that mean you know i finished it?
no. a wish to finish it does not tell us you did finish it. you could have stayed home and still needed more time.
use only our words and make the last answer shorter.
no. you said why you stayed home, not whether the book was finished.
what sentence could i add if i did finish it?
i finished the book before dinner.
can you know the dinner part from my first sentence?
no. that would be a new detail in the example. if you want only the fact about finishing, add: i finished the book.
i am talking with my friend, but i need a few minutes to think before answering her question. how can i say that without making her think i want her to go away?
you can say you want to give a real answer and need a short time to think. for example: i want to give you a real answer. can i think for a few minutes first?
give me just the short message.
i want to give you a real answer. can i think for a few minutes first?
what if she asks whether i am sad about something she did?
you can tell her what is true for you. asking for time to think does not always mean someone did something to make you feel sad.
i am not sad about her. i just need time.
then you could say: i am okay with you. i just need some time to think about the question.
can i say i will answer in one minute if i do not know that?
it is better not to give a specific time you may not keep. you can ask for a few minutes and let her know if you need longer.
write one kind sentence without a number.
i want to answer you, but i need a little time to think first.
here is a story: a woman left a book by a window. when she returned, it was on the table. she asked who moved it, but nobody answered. can you tell me who moved the book?
no. the story gives the change in place, but it does not give the person who moved it.
what if i say it was probably her brother?
that could be a new story idea, but nothing you gave makes her brother the answer. you have not even said he was there.
would the story be wrong if it stopped before she found out?
not always. a story can leave a question open. it would be wrong to say the answer is known when the story has not given it.
give me a more simple explanation.
a story can stop before every question has an answer. we can still say we do not know who moved the book.
what do we know for sure?
the woman left the book by the window and found it on the table when she returned.
write a question about that known detail.
where did she find the book when she returned?
on the table.
yes. that part is given in the story.
i told my friend i would meet her at the park, but now i want to meet at the library because it is cold. she has not answered my message yet.
until she answers, you do not know whether she has seen the new place. if you can, try to make sure she knows before leaving the first meeting place.
can you say she is wrong if she goes to the park?
not if the only plan she knows is the park. she could be using the plan you first gave.
say it another way.
she could go to the park because that is the plan she heard. she may not know you want to change it.
what should i write so it is clear i am asking for a change?
could we meet at the library instead because it is cold? please let me know if that works for you before i leave.
why not write we are meeting at the library now?
because you do not yet know that she has said yes. sending one message about your new choice does not tell us that she has chosen the same plan.
use only simple words and give me a short explanation.
you asked for a change, but she has not said yes yet.
i saw a small animal near the garden wall. can you tell me what it likes to eat?
not from small animal alone. food that works for one animal may not be right for another. i would need to know the kind before giving a specific answer.
keep the answer more simple.
the word animal is too general for that food question. i would need more information about which animal it is.
what can you say without knowing the kind?
i can keep the facts you gave: it was small and near the garden wall. those facts are not enough to tell us a specific food.
ask me a question about what i saw.
what else did you see about the animal?
i do not know any more details. write one sentence about it with no new facts.
you saw a small animal near the garden wall.
can a general word be useful even when it cannot answer every question?
yes. it can help us talk about what you saw, while leaving the details you do not know open.
my uncle keeps saying our visit is today, but the note we both read says tomorrow. i want to tell him what it says without making him feel wrong about everything.
you could keep the answer about the note rather than about him. for example: i checked the note again. it says tomorrow. shall we look at it together?
give me only the message.
i checked the note again, and it says tomorrow. shall we look at it together?
what if he says he has a new message changing it to today?
then you have new information to check. the old note may not be the whole plan now.
say that again in a more simple way.
then ask to see the new message. the old note may have been changed by a later plan.
should i keep saying tomorrow just because my note says it?
not if there is a real new message changing the day. the useful goal is to find the right plan, not to keep your first answer at any cost.
what could i say to him next?
could you show me the new message so we can check the day together?
write a story about someone waiting for a reply from a friend. let the reason for the wait be something simple.

a man asked a friend whether she would like to visit, but did not give a day. when no reply came that day, he thought she might not want to come. he sent another message asking about next week. later, she said she had been busy and would like to choose a day. he was happy to have her answer instead of making up one for her.
tell the story again in fewer words.
a man asked a friend to visit without giving a day. he felt worried when she did not answer. later, she said she had been busy and wanted to choose a day for the visit.
what did the first message leave out?
a day for the visit.
did no reply that day tell us she never wanted to visit?
no. later she said she had been busy and would like to choose a day.
use only simple words and ask me about something the story gives.
what did she want to choose when she answered?
a day.
yes, a day for the visit.
make this shorter without changing who did the work: my brother and i cleaned the kitchen after breakfast while our sister read by the window.
my brother and i cleaned the kitchen while our sister read.
can it say our sister cleaned the kitchen with us?
no. the original sentence says she was reading. adding her to the cleaning would change who did the work.
what if i want to leave my sister out of the short sentence?
you could say: my brother and i cleaned the kitchen after breakfast.
does leaving her out mean she was not there?
no. a short answer can leave out a detail without saying the opposite of it. the sentence about you and your brother does not tell us whether she was there.
write only a short answer that keeps who cleaned and where.
my brother and i cleaned the kitchen.
why did you keep my brother and i?
because you asked me to keep who did the cleaning. those words are the people who did it.
i read your explanation, but it is not clear to me yet. can you give an example instead of saying it the same way again?
yes. which part would you like an example for?
the difference between a wish to do something and having done it.
you might want to read a book this evening, but the book is not finished just because you want to read it. i want to read it is a wish. i have read it says the reading happened.
give me the two examples without the evening part.
i want to read the book is about a wish. i have read the book says you did the reading.
what if i started it but did not finish?
then you could say: i started reading the book, but i have not finished it yet.
can i use the same idea with writing a letter?
yes. i want to write a letter is a wish. i have written the letter says the writing is done.
give me only the example where the letter is started but not finished.
i started writing the letter, but i have not finished it yet.
what changed that helped me understand?
you asked for an example about another task instead of another long explanation.
my cousin asked if i can help with her school work. i have time for one question before i leave. how can i say yes without making it sound like i can stay all evening?
you can give both the yes and the time you have. for example: i can help with one question now, but then i need to leave.
just give me that sentence.
i can help with one question now, but then i need to leave.
she sends me a long list of questions. do i have to answer all of them because i said yes?
not from the yes you gave. you said you had time for one question. you can ask her which one she wants help with first.
write the reply.
i only have time for one question before i leave. which one would be most useful to work on now?
what if she says all of them are important?
you can understand that while still having the same time to help. you cannot make more time by saying the questions are important.
keep that answer more simple.
they can all be important, and you can still only have time for one question now.
i want to tell my sister about an old family visit, but i only remember the garden and a meal. i do not remember who cooked.
you can tell the parts you remember and leave the cooking as something you do not know. a story from memory does not need a made up answer for every detail.
write a simple start for me.
i remember sitting in the garden with our family and having a meal together. i do not remember who made the food.
should i say our grandmother cooked because she usually did?
you can say she often cooked, but that does not tell us she cooked on that visit. if you do not remember, keep that part open.
say it with know.
knowing she often cooked does not tell us she made that specific meal. you can say you do not know who cooked that day.
what if my sister says she can remember our father making it?
then she has a detail you can talk about together. you can say she has that memory of your father cooking, without saying you remember it yourself.
give me one sentence that keeps her information apart from my own memory.
my sister says our father made the meal, but i do not remember that part myself.
